title: India: Swaras & Shruti
tagline: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni
body: Seven swaras are India's solfège; only Sa and Pa are fixed. The octave divides into 22 shrutis. A tanpura drones Sa–Pa; gamaka ornaments make melody a continuous landscape.

title: India: Ragas & Thaats
body: A raga is a melodic rulebook: ascent, descent, signature phrases, mood, even time of day. Ten parent thaats organize hundreds of ragas — Yaman (evening, Lydian-like), Bhairav (dawn).

title: India: Tala
body: Tala is a repeating cycle of matras. Teentaal = 16 beats (4+4+4+4); sam, beat one, is the dramatic home. Layakari plays beat-divisions against the cycle.

title: Arabic Maqam
body: Maqam organizes Arabic melody with quarter tones. Rast = major with half-flat 3rd/7th; Bayati's half-flat 2nd; Hijaz's augmented 2nd. Maqamat stack tetrachords (jins); the taqsim explores them.

title: China: Wuyin Pentatonic
body: The five-tone wuyin ≈ Do Re Mi Sol La — no 4th or 7th, no semitones. Each tone can be home, giving five modes. Colours guqin, guzheng and folk melody.

title: Japan: Hirajoshi & Beyond
body: Japanese pentatonics are defined by semitone placement: Hirajoshi (koto), Yo (bright folk), In (melancholy), Iwato (dark). Koto, shakuhachi and gagaku carry them — with ma: expressive silence.

title: Indonesia: Gamelan
body: Gamelan tunes each ensemble uniquely — one 'body'. Slendro: five near-equal steps; pelog: seven uneven, five used. Bali interlocks kotekan; Java breathes courtly calm. Debussy heard it in 1889.

title: Korea: Gugak Foundations
body: Gugak splits into refined jeongak and folk minsogak. Modes live in sigimsae — required bends per degree; menarijo is the southwest lament. Gayageum, daegeum, haegeum, janggu.

title: Korea: Sanjo, Pansori & Jangdan
body: Sanjo: solo instrument with janggu accelerates through cycles. Pansori: one singer plus one drummer whose chuimsae shouts are rhythm and applause in one.

title: Persia: The Dastgah System
body: Persian classical music holds 12 systems: 7 dastgah plus 5 avaz. A dastgah is a mapped family of gushehs. The radif canonizes ~300 gushehs. Koron (half-flat) and sori notate the microtones.

title: Persia: Avaz & Tahrir
body: Dastgah performance is improvised within the map. Avaz is unmetered song framed by tasnif and chaharmezrab. Tahrir, the yodel-like break, crowns Persian singing.

title: Turkey: The Makam System
body: Turkish makam divides whole tones into 9 commas, walking tetrachords in a seyir. Rast, Ussak, Hicaz, Segah lead a fasıl; taksim improvises freely. Ney, tanbur, kanun, kemençe.

title: Turkey: Usul & Forms
body: Every Turkish piece rides a usul — düm and tek strokes from 2 beats to 120. Düyek (8) and aksak 9/8 (2+2+2+3) are everyday favourites.
